subject: cursor_plugins:skill:pstack/skills/poteto-mode#separate-fix-for-broken-skill
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-22 (conversation), rejections re-review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3: rejected again with a current reason. A skill found broken mid-task becomes its own bead, linked to its origin with discovered-from (.claude/skills/beads/references/prime.md:44; .claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/implement.md:259-260), and is built in its own worktree on its own branch (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/skill-curation.md:61). Per decision bead cr-0qcj, a pull request opens per feature or bug bead once it is implemented and verified, so that bead's fix already gets its own pull request without a skill-specific rule. The 2026-11-13 reason, that a pull request per fix assumes a review flow we do not run, is stale now Babysit and Shipping drive pull requests to merge (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/babysit.md:37-41; .claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/shipping.md:27-31).

why: Owner ruling 2026-11-22 (conversation), rejections re-review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3. The 2026-11-13 reason, that the wider rule makes the narrower list add nothing, no longer holds: Babysit pushes and replies under a standing grant (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/babysit.md:57-64) and Shipping merges and moves branches under another (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/shipping.md:35-40), and the Autopilot-full ruling grants committing, pushing to a working branch and opening a pull request without asking (ledger event 2026-11-20-deferred-playbooks:005), so a run acting under a grant needs the exceptions named. The target is doc:AGENTS.md, which README §5b lets hold a trait through its traits/ours.yaml entry and where authorization is set in one place (S-06); Babysit and Shipping cite the list when the bead delivers it.

subject: cursor_plugins:skill:pstack/skills/poteto-mode#draft-without-machine-patterns
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-22 (conversation), rejections re-review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3. Adopted, pending cr-r2pa.3.10: a modified adoption into edit-pass-before-posting, the owner's mechanism: text the Babysit and Shipping playbooks post for people to read passes through an unslop edit pass after it is drafted and before it is posted. Upstream's trait is different: it writes the reply free of the patterns while drafting and holds that a later cleanup pass does not remove them; the owner ruled the post-draft pass instead. Babysit posts review-thread replies (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/babysit.md:125-132) and Shipping posts its verdict as a pull-request comment (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/shipping.md:78-84); neither invokes unslop, which runs only where a unit calls it (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/plan.md:32; .claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/investigation.md:10). So the 2026-11-13 reason, that every reply a person reads already goes through unslop, no longer holds. The target is the Babysit playbook: one event names one target, Babysit posts the replies, and a playbook holds an adopted trait through its frontmatter (README §5b); Shipping's verdict text is routed by the same bead.
modification: Into `edit-pass-before-posting`. An unslop edit pass on the finished draft before Babysit or Shipping posts it, in place of writing without the patterns while drafting.

subject: cursor_plugins:skill:pstack/skills/poteto-mode#base-ref-fallback-and-fetch
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-22 (conversation), rejections re-review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3. Adopted, pending cr-r2pa.3.9: worktree-cleanup's audit judges merge state against a fetched base: the --base ref when given, else the remote default, else main or master with a warning, fetching it first and only warning when the fetch fails, so an offline run still finishes on the local ref. Today the audit takes --base, defaults to origin/HEAD and fetches nothing, to stay offline and read-only (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/worktree-cleanup.md:36-39; .claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/worktree-cleanup/audit.py:111; .claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/worktree-cleanup/audit.py:210). The owner adopted it with the merged-state signal and its offline fallback; Shipping already fetches trunk immediately before it judges ancestry (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/shipping.md:90-93).

subject: cursor_plugins:skill:pstack/skills/poteto-mode#pr-state-as-merge-signal
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-22 (conversation), rejections re-review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3. The 2026-11-13 reason was that the audit reads a squash merge as unmerged on purpose and needs no forge service (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/worktree-cleanup/audit.py:23-25; .claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/worktree-cleanup.md:36-39). The owner now accepts the forge read here; Shipping already reads a pull request's merged state back from the forge (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/shipping.md:99-100), the variant `also_in` lists.

subject: cursor_plugins:skill:pstack/skills/poteto-mode#remote-push-state
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-22 (conversation), rejections re-review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3. With the merged-state signal adopted beside it, a branch whose pull request merged on the forge can be proposed for removal although the base does not contain it, and whether its local commits reached the remote is what tells the owner nothing local is lost before approving (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/worktree-cleanup.md:47-51).

subject: cursor_plugins:skill:pstack/automations/benny/skills/reproduce-and-fix-issues#repro-budget-outcomes
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-22 (conversation), rejections re-review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3. subject: cursor_plugins:skill:pstack/automations/benny/skills/reproduce-and-fix-issues#independent-media-review
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-22 (conversation), rejections re-review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3: rejected again with a current reason. subject: cursor_plugins:skill:pstack/automations/benny/skills/triage-issue-reports#duplicate-search-key-list

subject: cursor_plugins:skill:pstack/skills/why#full-coverage-search
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-22 (conversation), rejections re-review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3: rejected again with a current reason. The 2026-11-01 reason rested on the repository having few local sources; that is gone, since why now searches each outside source a project marks available (.claude/skills/why/SKILL.md:37-46). The real reason is that a why run stays bounded by its question, and its tiers rate each claim by its own evidence (.claude/skills/why/SKILL.md:61-72). why already searches each source the project marks have (.claude/skills/why/SKILL.md:40-43) and names every source searched, empty or skipped, with the reason (.claude/skills/why/SKILL.md:91-92). What this trait adds is searching an unpromising source as an aim in itself, toward a complete coverage map, which the bounded run does not take on.

subject: cursor_plugins:skill:pstack/skills/why#category-strength-map
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-22 (conversation), rejections re-review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3: rejected again with a current reason. The 2026-11-01 reason was that the map needs fixed source categories, which explain-code did not keep; why now keeps a fixed list of outside source kinds (.claude/skills/why/references/outside-sources.md:21-27), so that part is gone. Upstream's roster tells each investigator what kind of motive its source category is best placed to reveal and when it is strongest, so it knows what to expect and can name a gap when a category comes back empty. Ours already gives each outside source its own motive cue, in that source's section (.claude/skills/why/references/outside-sources.md:60-61; .claude/skills/why/references/outside-sources.md:77-78), which a run follows for each source the project marks available (.claude/skills/why/SKILL.md:37-46), and a source searched empty or skipped goes on the Sources line with its reason (.claude/skills/why/SKILL.md:91-92). A why run stays bounded by its question, so a cue arriving with the source it describes is enough; a separate map across every category would add a list to read on each run and nothing the per-source cues lack.

subject: cursor_plugins:skill:pstack/skills/why#provable-irrelevance-bar
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-22 (conversation), rejections re-review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3: rejected again with a current reason. subject: cursor_plugins:skill:pstack/skills/why#fresh-synthesizer
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-22 (conversation), rejections re-review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3: rejected again with a current reason. The real reason is that a why run stays bounded by its question, and its tiers rate each claim by its own evidence (.claude/skills/why/SKILL.md:61-72). why gathers everything before it settles on an answer, forming no conclusion while gathering (.claude/skills/why/SKILL.md:28-29), then judges and answers; a delegate works under the same read-only limit (.claude/skills/why/SKILL.md:14-15), and the coordinator integrates what delegates return (AGENTS.md:51-52). subject: cursor_plugins:skill:pstack/skills/why#human-followup-pointer
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-22 (conversation), rejections re-review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3: rejected again with a current reason. subject: mattpocock_skills:skill:skills/engineering/setup-matt-pocock-skills#pr-as-issue
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-22 (conversation), rejections re-review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3. The reference check fails a pull request with no issue reference (docs/specs/2026-11-20-beads-github-mirror.md:58-59) and outside contributors cannot create beads; the mirror's digest lists such a pull request for triage (docs/specs/2026-11-20-beads-github-mirror.md:221), and triage today tracks the issue a pull request names, or fixes the reference through pr, or dismisses the row (.claude/skills/triage/SKILL.md:92-97). The target is triage, which tracker sends the digest's untracked rows to (.claude/skills/tracker/SKILL.md:134-136). The 2026-11-09 premise, that a hosted pull-request rule has nothing to attach to, is gone.
